title: Cairo to Luxor and Aswan: Train, Bus or Flight?
excerpt: Cairo to Luxor compared: sleeper train, day train, Go Bus or flight, with real times, dated fares and stations, and when flying wins.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

The quick answer

Flying from Cairo to Luxor takes about an hour in the air against roughly 10 to 11 hours by day train or bus, so flying wins when time is short. The overnight sleeper saves a hotel night and reaches Luxor at 06:10 on the quickest service. The day train shows you the Nile Valley, and the Go Bus costs least. Cairo to Aswan works the same way, with about three and a half hours added overland, or a flight of about an hour and 20 minutes.

Check Abela Trains directly for current sleeper services, departure stations, fares and booking availability.

Luxor is a long way south of Cairo, with Aswan about 215 km further on, and every traveller has to cross that distance at least once, by air, overnight sleeper, daytime train or bus. The choice shapes your whole itinerary: it decides whether you arrive with a full Luxor day ahead or lose one in transit. This post compares real journey times, dated fares, stations and booking routes, then ends with a clear recommendation. Sawa Tours (sawa.tours) is an Egypt shared-departure marketplace whose team has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993, and its nine-day Cairo-and-cruise package includes both domestic flights.

Cairo to Luxor: the short answer

Fly from Cairo to Luxor when time is short: about an hour in the air against 10 to 11 hours by rail or road. Take the overnight sleeper when you would rather travel while you sleep, because it saves a hotel night and reaches Luxor around 06:10. The day train trades speed for Nile Valley scenery; the Go Bus is the low-budget workhorse. For Cairo to Aswan, add about three and a half hours to any overland option, or fly in about an hour and 20 minutes.

Cairo to Luxor and Aswan: times, fares and comfort compared

Four realistic options cover the route. Rail fares are the foreigner prices published by Seat 61 (page last updated 14 September 2026, checked 8 November 2026). Bus and flight figures come from 12Go's listing, viewed on 8 November 2026, and are indicative only: aggregators add their own margin and the page's own figures were inconsistent in places.

Sleeper train (Abela) Bashtil 19:45 and Giza 20:15, Luxor 06:10, Aswan 09:25 US$110 sharing, US$150 sole; Elite US$125 and US$170 Private two-berth cabin with dinner and breakfast; book on abelatrains.com or the Abela app, at an Abela office or through an agency

If you want a recommendation: on a first visit, fly Cairo to Luxor, because the half day you save is worth more than the fare gap. Take the sleeper when the overnight run saves a hotel night, the day train for the scenery, the bus for the smallest budget. Most itineraries only need one long leg: Cairo to Luxor first, then work south and fly home from Aswan.

Six details most fare tables miss

  • Mind the station. "Cairo" means more than one. The VIP day train 980 leaves Cairo Ramses, while the sleepers leave Cairo Upper Egypt (Bashtil), with a later stop at Giza. Some other Upper Egypt services also use Bashtil, so read the station name on your ticket and tell your driver the station, not just "the train station".
  • Foreigners pay dollar fares. Foreigner prices, set in US dollars or euros, have applied on Egyptian trains since December 2022. The national railway's website and app sell Egyptian-price tickets to Egyptians only; foreigners can use them to check times.
  • Know the booking windows. Sleepers open four to five months ahead. Day-train bookings open about two weeks before departure, and agencies need at least two days' notice.
  • Carry cash. Seat 61 recommends crisp US dollar or euro notes. The foreigner office at Ramses takes cards with a 2.5% fee, and the tourist windows at Luxor and Aswan may or may not.
  • Expect checkpoints. Police check ID regularly in Egypt, and you may be detained if you cannot show your passport and visa (FCDO, 27 October 2026). Keep your passport with you, not in the hold.
  • Think about the return. The classic loop goes overland or by air to Luxor, moves south, then flies Aswan to Cairo, so you never repeat the desert.

The overnight sleeper train to Luxor and Aswan

The sleeper is the overnight hotel on wheels run by Abela Trains, which took over from the Watania service in August 2023, and it is the classic overland route south. Train 86 leaves Cairo Upper Egypt station at 19:45, calls at Giza at 20:15, reaches Luxor at 06:10 and Aswan at 09:25. Train 82 leaves 85 minutes later and reaches Luxor at 07:50 and Aswan at 11:10. Each traveller gets a berth in a private two-berth cabin, or a one-berth cabin, with bedding, a washbasin, an evening meal and breakfast.

  1. Fares. Standard cabin: US$110 per person sharing, US$150 sole occupancy. Elite: US$125 sharing, US$170 sole, with a power socket by each berth. Children aged 4 to 9 pay US$70, and children under 4 travel free without a berth (Seat 61, 2026 fares).
  2. Stations. Sleepers leave from Cairo Upper Egypt (Bashtil), in west Greater Cairo with no direct metro link, and call at Giza, which is reached by metro and suits travellers based near the pyramids.
  3. Booking. Book on abelatrains.com or the Abela app, at an Abela office (Ramses, Cairo Upper Egypt, Giza, Luxor and Aswan), or through 12Go, Bookaway or Trains Egypt. Berths sell out well ahead in December and January.
  4. The trade-off. A 06:10 Luxor arrival is long before hotel check-in. Plan breakfast, or ask your hotel about an early check-in.

The day train down the Nile Valley

Egyptian National Railways runs daytime trains south, and the ride is a moving window on rural Egypt, with the river itself in view for much of the way. The VIP train 980 leaves Cairo Ramses at 08:00, reaches Luxor at 18:55 and Aswan at 22:25, which is about 11 hours to Luxor and 14.5 hours to Aswan. Train 2010 leaves Ramses at 10:00 and reaches Luxor at 19:30. A traveller on Seat 61 reported the express taking "10 hours or so".

  • Trains and classes. Talgo trains, introduced in 2023, are the top class, followed by VIP Express and the Russian-built cars, which have replaced most older second and third-class cars on this route. Seat 61 lists Cairo to Luxor at US$85 first or US$75 second on the Talgo, US$75 or US$55 on VIP or Express, and US$75, US$47 or US$41 for Russian second, third air-conditioned and third non-air-conditioned. Cairo to Aswan runs higher: US$95 or US$90 on the Talgo and US$80 or US$65 on VIP or Express.
  • Timing. The morning departure reaches Luxor in the evening, so it costs a sightseeing day. It suits travellers with spare days or a dislike of overnight travel.
  • Buying tickets. Use the foreigner office upstairs at Ramses, or order through an agency such as 12Go or Bookaway, which deliver hard-copy tickets to your hotel. Expect the agency price to run higher: 12Go listed Cairo to Luxor trains from about US$73 on 8 November 2026, against Seat 61's published foreigner fares from US$41.

Flying from Cairo to Luxor and Aswan

Flying is the only option measured in minutes. The air time is about 1 hour 5 to 10 minutes to Luxor and about 1 hour 20 to 25 minutes to Aswan; an EgyptAir Cairo to Aswan flight (MS 286) is scheduled at 1 hour 20 minutes. Add transfers and airport security and the door-to-door trip is still much shorter than any overland option. The trade-offs: fares move with the season (12Go showed a wide range on 8 November 2026), domestic baggage allowances are modest, and you should check which Cairo terminal your airline uses, since EgyptAir flies from Terminal 3 and other airlines may differ.

The bus to Luxor and Aswan: Go Bus times and fares

The Go Bus is the budget pick: reclining air-conditioned seats in several classes, and the lowest fares of the four, from about US$13 for Cairo to Luxor in the 12Go listing of 8 November 2026. Count about 10 to 11 hours. Super Jet runs a parallel network. The honest downsides: the desert highway offers none of the train's views, rest stops are brief, and a 10-hour bus after a long-haul flight is a hard combination. The FCDO notes that serious bus crashes have occurred and advises against driving outside main cities and resorts at night, so weigh a night coach against a daytime one or the sleeper.

Cairo to Aswan: what changes on the longer route

Cairo to Aswan is the same journey with Aswan about 215 km beyond Luxor, and every overland option takes roughly three and a half hours longer than to Luxor. The sleeper's 09:25 arrival is its trump card: you travel, sleep, breakfast on board and step off with most of the day ahead. For guided sightseeing, the Aswan Highlights tour (from €36 per person, as listed in November 2026, hotel pickup included) is easiest booked for the following day. Flying saves the most time; the day train's 14.5 hours are a hard sell beyond Luxor.

The Luxor to Aswan short hop

Most travellers never ride Cairo to Aswan in one go: they stop in Luxor first. The last leg is then easy. Daytime trains cover it in about three and a half hours, and foreigner fares run from US$26 to US$77 depending on train and class. The cheapest seat is on the sleeper trains 86 and 87 in seat mode, at US$10 (Seat 61, 2026 fares). The slow alternative is a Nile cruise, which turns a transfer day into Edfu, Kom Ombo and the river itself.

The verdict: train, bus or flight?

For most first-time visitors: fly Cairo to Luxor, take the sleeper if the overnight appeals, keep the bus for the tightest budgets, and treat Cairo to Aswan as the same choice with three and a half hours added. Every fare here is dated, so re-check before paying. Next step: see the Egypt in Depth 9-day package with both flights included, or browse forming departures on Sawa. Reserving a seat costs nothing.

meta_description: Cairo to Luxor compared: sleeper train, day train, Go Bus or flight, with real times, dated fares and stations, and when flying wins.
tldr: Flying from Cairo to Luxor takes about an hour in the air against roughly 10 to 11 hours by day train or bus, so flying wins when time is short. The overnight sleeper saves a hotel night and reaches Luxor at 06:10 on the quickest service. The day train shows you the Nile Valley, and the Go Bus costs least. Cairo to Aswan works the same way, with about three and a half hours added overland, or a flight of about an hour and 20 minutes.

faq.q: How far is Aswan from Cairo?
faq.a: Aswan is about 215 km beyond Luxor. By air it is about an hour and 20 minutes from Cairo. Overland, count on about 14.5 hours on the day train and a 09:25 arrival on the quickest sleeper. Most travellers break the journey in Luxor, then cover the final stretch by cruise, train or the sleeper in seat mode.

faq.q: Is the overnight sleeper train safe for solo female travellers?
faq.a: Cabins are private compartments, and a solo traveller can book a one-berth cabin or one bed in a two-berth cabin shared with a passenger of the same gender. Keep valuables close and confirm your platform before boarding. As on any train in Egypt, the FCDO notes that fatal train collisions and derailments have occurred, so treat it as normal-risk travel.

faq.q: Do Cairo to Luxor trains sell out, and how early should I book?
faq.a: In peak season, yes. Sleepers open four to five months ahead and foreigners book through Abela's site or app, an Abela office or an agency. Day-train bookings open about two weeks before departure. If trains are full, the Go Bus is the fallback, and flights rarely sell out entirely.

faq.q: Which Cairo station do trains to Luxor leave from?
faq.a: It depends on the train. The VIP day train 980 starts at Cairo Ramses; the overnight sleeper leaves from Cairo Upper Egypt (Bashtil) with its own Giza stop, and some other Upper Egypt services also use Bashtil. Check the station on your ticket and tell the driver its name, because "the train station" is an ambiguous address in Cairo.

faq.q: Can I take a train from Luxor to Aswan instead of a cruise?
faq.a: Yes, and it is the easy leg: about three and a half hours by day train, with foreigner fares from US$26 to US$77 depending on class, or US$10 in seat mode on sleeper trains 86 and 87. The cruise is the scenic alternative, turning a transfer day into Edfu, Kom Ombo and time on the river.

faq.q: How much is the flight from Cairo to Luxor?
faq.a: It varies widely with season and booking time. On 8 November 2026 an aggregator (12Go) listed Cairo to Luxor flights from about US$88 to US$327, with some schedule fares near US$50. At about an hour in the air it is the only option that leaves a full day for sightseeing, which is why most short itineraries pay for it. Check the airline for the current fare.

faq.q: What happens if my Sawa departure never fills?
faq.a: Nothing is charged. A shared departure is confirmed when four travellers have reserved it, and no card is involved before that moment. A day tour has until seven days before departure to reach four, and a package until 30 days before; if a date misses, it is cancelled, nothing is charged and Sawa suggests another date. Once a date is confirmed it is not cancelled for low numbers. If you are combining separate departures, book flights and trains only after each date confirms.
